Definition: from G2117 and G1408; to lay a straight course, i.e. sail direct:--(come) with a straight course.
BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, euthydroméō is the word for (come) with a straight course. In Acts 16:11, the text says "we came with a straight course to Samothracia."
TheologicalSignificance: For me, euthydroméō means with a straight course, and I leave it at that.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
